Composite bundles <math> Y\to \Sigma \to X</math> play a prominent role in [[gauge theory]] with [[symmetry breaking]], e.g., [[gauge gravitation theory]], [[non-autonomous mechanics]] where <math>X=\mathbb R</math> is the time axis, e.g., mechanics with time-dependent parameters, and so on. There are the important relations between [[connection (fibred manifold)|connections]] on [[fiber bundle]]s <math>Y\to X</math>, <math>Y\to \Sigma</math> and <math>\Sigma\to X</math>.

==Composite bundle==

In [[differential geometry]] by a '''composite bundle''' is meant the composition

: <math>\pi: Y\to \Sigma\to X  \qquad\qquad (1)</math>

of fiber bundles

: <math>\pi_{Y\Sigma}: Y\to\Sigma, \qquad  \pi_{\Sigma X}: \Sigma\to X. </math>

It is provided with bundle coordinates <math>(x^\lambda,\sigma^m,y^i) </math>, where <math> (x^\lambda,\sigma^m) </math> are bundle coordinates on a fiber bundle <math>\Sigma\to X</math>, i.e., transition functions of coordinates <math>\sigma^m</math> are independent of coordinates <math>y^i</math>.

The following fact provides the above-mentioned physical applications of composite bundles. Given the composite bundle (1), let <math>h</math> be a global section
of a fiber bundle <math>\Sigma\to X</math>, if any. Then the [[pullback bundle]] 
<math>Y^h=h^*Y</math> over <math>X</math> is a subbundle of a fiber bundle <math>Y\to X</math>.

==Composite principal bundle ==

For instance, let <math>P\to X</math> be a [[principal bundle]] with a structure Lie group <math>G</math> which is [[reduction of the structure group|reducible]] to its closed subgroup <math>H</math>. There is a composite bundle <math>P\to P/H\to X</math> where <math>P\to P/H</math> is a principal bundle with a structure group <math>H</math> and <math>P/H\to X</math> is a fiber bundle associated with <math>P\to X</math>. Given a global section <math>h</math> of <math>P/H\to X</math>, the pullback bundle <math>h^*P</math> is a reduced principal subbundle of <math>P</math> with a structure group <math>H</math>. In [[gauge theory]], sections of <math>P/H\to X</math> are treated as [[Higgs field (classical)|classical Higgs fields]].

== Jet manifolds of a composite bundle==

Given the composite bundle <math>Y\to \Sigma\to X</math> (1), consider the [[jet bundle|jet manifolds]] <math>J^1\Sigma</math>, <math>J^1_\Sigma Y</math>, and <math>J^1Y</math> of the fiber bundles <math>\Sigma\to X</math>, <math>Y\to \Sigma</math>, and <math>Y\to X</math>, respectively. They are provided with the adapted coordinates <math> ( x^\lambda,\sigma^m, \sigma^m_\lambda) </math>, <math> (x^\lambda, \sigma^m, y^i, \widehat  y^i_\lambda, y^i_m), </math>, and <math>(x^\lambda, \sigma^m, y^i, \sigma^m_\lambda ,y^i_\lambda). </math>

There is the canonical map

: <math> J^1\Sigma\times_\Sigma J^1_\Sigma Y\to_Y J^1Y, \qquad
y^i_\lambda=y^i_m \sigma^m_\lambda +\widehat y^i_\lambda</math>.

==Composite connection==

This canonical map  defines the relations between connections on fiber bundles <math>Y\to X</math>, <math>Y\to\Sigma</math> and <math>\Sigma\to X</math>. These connections are given by the corresponding [[connection (fibred manifold)|tangent-valued connection forms]]

: <math>\gamma=dx^\lambda\otimes (\partial_\lambda +\gamma_\lambda^m\partial_m + \gamma_\lambda^i\partial_i), </math>

: <math>  A_\Sigma=dx^\lambda\otimes (\partial_\lambda + A_\lambda^i\partial_i) +d\sigma^m\otimes (\partial_m + A_m^i\partial_i), </math>

: <math> \Gamma=dx^\lambda\otimes (\partial_\lambda + \Gamma_\lambda^m\partial_m). </math>

A connection <math>A_\Sigma</math> on a fiber bundle <math>Y\to\Sigma</math>
and a connection <math>\Gamma</math>  on a fiber bundle <math>\Sigma\to
X</math> define a connection

: <math> \gamma=dx^\lambda\otimes (\partial_\lambda +\Gamma_\lambda^m\partial_m + (A_\lambda^i +
A_m^i\Gamma_\lambda^m)\partial_i) </math>

on a composite bundle <math>Y\to X</math>. It is called the '''composite connection'''. This is a unique connection such that the [[connection (fibred manifold)|horizontal lift]] <math>\gamma\tau </math> onto <math>Y</math> of a vector field <math>\tau</math> on <math>X</math> by means of the composite connection <math>\gamma</math> coincides with the composition <math>A_\Sigma(\Gamma\tau) </math> of horizontal lifts of <math>\tau</math> onto <math>\Sigma</math> by means of a connection <math>\Gamma</math> and then onto <math>Y</math> by means of a connection <math>A_\Sigma</math>.

==Vertical covariant differential==

Given the composite bundle <math>Y</math> (1), there is the following [[exact sequence]] of vector bundles over <math>Y</math>:

: <math> 0\to V_\Sigma Y\to VY\to Y\times_\Sigma V\Sigma\to 0, \qquad\qquad (2)</math>

where <math>V_\Sigma Y</math>  and <math>V_\Sigma^*Y</math> are the [[vertical bundle|vertical tangent bundle]]  and the [[connection (fibred manifold)|vertical cotangent bundle]] of <math>Y\to\Sigma</math>. Every connection <math>A_\Sigma</math> on a fiber bundle <math>Y\to\Sigma</math> yields the splitting

: <math>A_\Sigma: TY\supset VY \ni \dot y^i\partial_i + \dot\sigma^m\partial_m \to (\dot
y^i -A^i_m\dot\sigma^m)\partial_i </math>

of the exact sequence (2). Using this splitting, one can construct a first order [[differential operator]]

: <math> \widetilde D: J^1Y\to T^*X\otimes_Y V_\Sigma Y, \qquad \widetilde D= dx^\lambda\otimes(y^i_\lambda- A^i_\lambda -A^i_m\sigma^m_\lambda)\partial_i, </math>

on a composite bundle <math>Y\to X</math>. It is called the '''vertical covariant differential'''.
It possesses the following important property.

Let <math>h</math> be a section of a fiber bundle <math>\Sigma\to X</math>, and let <math>h^*Y\subset Y</math> be the pullback bundle over <math>X</math>. Every connection <math>A_\Sigma</math> induces the [[connection (fibred manifold)|pullback connection]]

: <math>A_h=dx^\lambda\otimes[\partial_\lambda+((A^i_m\circ h)\partial_\lambda h^m
+(A\circ h)^i_\lambda)\partial_i] </math>

on <math>h^*Y</math>. Then the restriction of a vertical covariant differential <math>\widetilde D</math>  to <math>J^1h^*Y\subset J^1Y</math> coincides with the familiar [[connection (fibred manifold)|covariant differential]] <math>D^{A_h}</math>
on <math>h^*Y</math> relative to the pullback connection <math>A_h</math>.
